text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
- Opposition parties and farming groups urged the government to make public its plans for developng the agricultural sector, following a conference at the headquarters of oppositon party Fidesz.
- The opposition Christian Democrat leader Gyorgy Giczy said a proposal by fellow opposition party the Democratic Forum to form an alliance was "not timely".

- Privatisation minister Judit Csiha is set to propose an amendment to the privatisation law to ensure that the state only keeps stakes in companies when it is really necessary for the nation's secirity.

- Socialist MP Judit Csehak said revelations by a screening panel that she had had access to security documents while a member of the last communist government before 1990 was "not something I should be ashamed of".
- The income and expenditure of state privatisation agency APV amounted to 11.02 billion and 4.48 billion forints respectively in the first two months of 1997.
- Magyar Hitel Bank is expected to decide on Tuesday to reinvest all of its three billion forints 1996 post-tax profits

- Socialist MP Gabor Kiss, who was implicated in the "Operation Birch Tree" scandal in which security services illegally gathered information on Socialist MPs, has agreed to resign at the end of the present parliament in 1998.
